name: Rice – Wheat
description: Dominant crop rotation across the Indo-Gangetic Plains covering over 70% of irrigated land in Bihar.
benefits: High staple calorie security
Well-established government Minimum Support Price (MSP) procurement channels
risks: Depletes groundwater reserves where tubewell irrigation is over-extracted
Perpetuates Poaceae monoculture encouraging Phalaris minor and spot blotch build-up
Leaves land bare from late March to June (zaid) exposing soil to high solar radiation and organic matter burn-off
Terminal heat stress on wheat during March grain filling

source_notes.agronomy: ICAR-RCER Patna Indo-Gangetic Plains Cereal Systems Review.
source_notes.fallow_risk: CIMMYT CSISA Bihar Cropping Systems Diagnostics.

name: Rice – Rabi Maize
description: High-yielding cash grain system highly popular in North Bihar alluvial zones (Begusarai, Khagaria, Samastipur).
benefits: Significantly higher profit margins and grain yields compared to rabi wheat
High stover biomass for dairy forage or mulch
risks: Heavy nitrogen and potassium mining requiring balanced fertilizer management
Late harvest of rabi maize can delay summer field preparation

source_notes.agronomy: BAU Sabour Rabi Maize Production Manual & ICAR-IIMR.

name: Rice – Lentil (Paira / Zero-Till)
description: Resource-conserving rotation suited for water-stressed tracts or lowlands with residual post-monsoon soil moisture.
benefits: Biological nitrogen fixation saves synthetic N for next season
Low irrigation requirement (often grown rainfed on residual moisture)
High market price and local household dietary protein
risks: Vulnerable to collar rot or seedling damping-off if excess moisture persists post-harvest
Susceptible to Pod borer and Stemphylium blight under sudden humid foggy conditions

source_notes.agronomy: ICAR-IIPR Kanpur Relay/Paira Cropping in Rice Fallows & BAU Sabour.

name: Rice – Mustard
description: Cereal-oilseed rotation breaking graminaceous weed cycles with low irrigation requirement.
benefits: Requires only 2-3 light irrigations, saving substantial groundwater
Mustard root glucosinolate residues act as natural biofumigants against soil pathogens
Ready cash return from edible oil market
risks: Sensitive to winter cold waves / frost during early siliqua formation
Severe yield drop if aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) infestation goes unchecked

source_notes.agronomy: ICAR-DRMR Bharatpur & BAU Sabour Oilseeds Program.

name: Kharif Maize – Wheat / Chickpea
description: Upland Bihar rotation replacing high-water puddle rice with upland maize followed by drought-tolerant pulses.
benefits: Cuts total water consumption by 40-50% compared to puddled rice systems
Improves soil structure by eliminating wet puddling pans
risks: Kharif maize requires excellent field drainage; prone to waterlogging death during heavy monsoon downpours

source_notes.agronomy: CIMMYT Sustainable Intensification Program in Eastern India.

name: Rice – Wheat – Summer Moong (Intensified Legume)
description: Triple-cropping system that covers the bare summer (zaid) gap with an early maturing 60-day pulse.
benefits: Eliminates the bare-field period during zaid, reducing soil erosion and solar organic carbon loss
Fixes 30-40 kg N/ha and yields 8-12 q/ha high-value pulse grain
Stover can be incorporated as green mulch right before rice puddling
risks: Requires assured tubewell irrigation (2-3 irrigations in April-May)
Tight turnaround window between wheat harvest (April) and rice transplanting (June-July)

source_notes.agronomy: ICAR-RCER Patna Cereal-Legume Intensification Protocol & BAU Sabour.

name: Green Manure (Dhaincha) – Rice – Lentil
description: Ecological soil-rebuilding strategy optimizing biological nitrogen, soil organic matter, and minimal groundwater extraction.
benefits: Dual legume components supply up to 100-140 kg N/ha biological fertility
Increases soil water holding capacity and buffers against both monsoon breaks and terminal heat
Lowest chemical input cost among all rotations
risks: Dhaincha must be incorporated at exactly 45-50 days before succulent stems turn woody
Requires rotavator or power tiller for timely biomass burial

source_notes.agronomy: ICAR-CSSRI Karnal Green Manure Systematics & BAU Sabour.

name: Makhana – Rabi Wheat / Lentil
description: Field-based wetland rotation turning chronically waterlogged kharif lowlands into high-value superfood production followed by winter grain.
benefits: Exceptional economic returns from GI-tagged Mithila Makhana
Thrives in lowlands where conventional crops drown during monsoon
risks: Specialized labor required for traditional seed collection from pond/field bed
Field de-watering infrastructure needed prior to rabi sowing

source_notes.agronomy: ICAR-RCER Research Centre on Makhana, Darbhanga: Field-based Makhana Cultivation.
